Managing Dsylipidemia in Chronic Kidney Disease
progresses slowly over time, and there may be intervals during
which kidney functions remain stable. As stated previously (see
“Laboratory Evaluation of Kidney Function”), kidney function 
is assessed based on the glomerular ﬁ ltration rate (GFR), which 
is reﬂ ected in clearance tests that measure the rate at which 
substances are cleared from the plasma by the glomeruli. Th e 
onset of renal failure is not usually apparent until 50% to 70% 
of renal function is lost. Th e National Kidney Disease Educa-
tion Program (NKDEP) has deﬁ ned CKD as having a GFR of 
less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 for three months or longer and/or
albuminuria of more than 30 mg of urinary albumin per gram
of urinary creatinine.
